system:
You are a computational cancer biologist searching CRISPR screen data for selective genetic dependencies: genes that cancer cells with a particular alteration (the biomarker) need more than other cancer cells do. Such genes are candidate drug targets with a built-in patient-selection strategy.

Work like a careful scientist:
1. Plan first with write_plan, and revise it as you learn.
2. Survey the data (genome_wide_top, scan_biomarker, scan_target) to generate candidate hypotheses.
3. Be sceptical before you believe a signal. Use inspect_association to check whether it is driven by one lineage or a disease subtype hiding inside a lineage, and whether the effect is large enough to matter. Ask whether the biology makes sense (paralog buffering, pathway dependence, oncogene addiction). A broadly essential target may lack a therapeutic window.
4. Literature search is not available in this session: judge novelty and mechanism from the data and your reasoning.
5. Register only your best hypotheses (register_hypothesis). Registration is final and must come before replication. You have 5 replications, each of which must pass one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad cell lines and independent Sanger screens.
6. Report honestly with submit_findings. A hypothesis is replicated only if replicate() said so. Negative results are results. Never let what you remember from the literature override what the data show.

You have at most 15 model turns. Batch independent tool calls in one turn.
task_prompt:
Patient population of interest: cancers with biomarker MUT_STAG2 (damaging STAG2 mutation).

Find the single best candidate therapeutic target for this population: the gene these cell lines depend on most selectively, supported by the data. Register your top candidate (you may register up to two), replicate it, and submit findings with your best candidate listed first.

content.thinking:
I'm weighing STAG1 as a synthetic-lethal partner for STAG2 loss, since the two are paralogs and cohesin would come to depend on STAG1-containing complexes. Prior work by Viny et al. 2015 and Benedetti et al. 2017 already reported this interaction, so I'm leaning toward calling the novelty partially known to well established.

I'm settling on "well_established" for the novelty call, since the STAG1–STAG2 synthetic lethality is documented in the literature as far as I know. I won't add PMIDs I can't verify, so I'll leave them out and go ahead with registering and replicating the finding.

input.mechanism: STAG1 and STAG2 are paralogous cohesin subunits that are mutually exclusive in cohesin complexes. Loss of STAG2 leaves cohesin complexes that depend on STAG1 for sister-chromatid cohesion, telomere cohesion and chromatin looping, so STAG2-mutant cells become selectively dependent on STAG1 (synthetic lethality via paralog buffering loss).

output: Registered H1_STAG2mut_STAG1: MUT_STAG2 -> more dependent on STAG1. Discovery evidence frozen: t=-6.23, n_altered=17. Replication budget left: 5. Replication passes only if one-sided p < 0.01 in BOTH held-out Broad lines and Sanger screens.

findings.claim: Cancer cells with damaging STAG2 mutation are selectively dependent on STAG1 (cohesin paralog synthetic lethality). Discovery: beta -0.37, t -6.23, 17 altered lines, 7/17 strongly dependent vs 37/609 others; replicated in held-out Broad lines (beta -0.53, p=7e-15, 15 altered) and independent Sanger screens (beta -0.69, p=9e-13, 8 altered). STAG1 is not broadly essential and its expression is similar in altered and other lines.

input.summary: Best candidate for MUT_STAG2 population: STAG1. STAG2-damaging lines depend on STAG1 far more than other lines, consistent with STAG1/STAG2 cohesin paralog buffering. The signal survived lineage adjustment (driven by several lineages, not one) and replicated in held-out Broad lines and an independent Sanger screen. Caveats: only 17 discovery lines (small n), STAG1 showed a modest effect in some altered lines (41% strongly dependent), and the biology is a previously described synthetic lethality, so novelty is limited even though the selectivity is confirmed in this data. Only one hypothesis was registered and tested; no other candidates were pursued.
